version.changelog: Just ask your agent: human-friendly listing, natural-language examples, context-first runtime/profile guidance, focused questions only when needed, and technical commands moved to an on-demand reference. Audits remain read-only.

llm.summary: This skill appears to be a disclosed, read-only token and cost auditing helper rather than something that changes settings or collects credentials.

dimensions.detail: Live OpenClaw mode runs fixed native read commands and may contact configured services or update native caches; this is disclosed and proportionate to auditing model status and scheduled jobs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is via normal ClawHub skill installation or a documented clawhub install command; I found no install hooks, auto-start behavior, dependency installation, or remote payload retrieval.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions repeatedly scope activity to read-only checks, explicit runtime/profile evidence, no installs, no recursive home searches, no credential reads, and no raw config output.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package does not write configuration, create jobs, modify schedules, install persistence, or store reports; selected local files and native read results are processed in-process and summarized.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to inspect OpenClaw or Hermes token/cost efficiency and recommend next steps; the scripts implement audit, context sizing, budget summary, and model-route eligibility checks without activating models or applying changes.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable letting the agent run local read-only OpenClaw diagnostics and read explicitly selected config/profile files. Review generated reports before sharing them, because model names, agent IDs, filenames, and findings can still reveal private operational details.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The flagged wrapper scripts insert legacy subcommands such as route, budget, context, and audit, but README, CHANGELOG, QUICKSTART, and SECURITY.md disclose them as migration shims and the target commands are diagnostic.
[PE3] unexpected: The .env references are prohibitions and safety statements; hermes_adapter.py and the docs say .env and credentials are not read, and I found no code path that loads credential stores.
[LP3] expected: The skill relies on host tool permissions plus natural-language boundaries rather than manifest-level allowed-tools, but the requested Python/OpenClaw/local-file access is scoped and disclosed for a local audit.
[EA2] expected: The phrase about proceeding without asking applies only when trusted host context already identifies the runtime/profile; ambiguous cases instruct the agent to ask instead of guessing.
[SDI-4] expected: The wrapper docstrings are imprecise because they insert a subcommand, but the behavior is documented elsewhere as compatibility shims and does not add mutation or hidden privilege.
[AST4] expected: optimizer.py uses subprocess.run with a fixed openclaw executable, argv lists, no shell, timeout, and fixed read commands; this is expected for native OpenClaw auditing.
[OH3] expected: The cited 'no truncation' text is a report caveat, while file and native-response reads are capped at 8 MiB and reports omit raw file contents.
[aig-skill-scan] expected: The supplied SARIF run reported no results; the package contents were still inspected directly rather than relying on the empty scan alone.
